title: Games that using AI chatting, beware the neg reviews and api bill black hole
author: dotdashgames2
selftext:
We know that, beyond AI-generated assets (art, music, etc.) and AI-assisted programming, there is another, more direct service-oriented AI application: embedding large models into games so that players can converse with AI NPCs or use AI to provide information. But games of this kind all share one worry—the API costs.

Recently, DeepSeek tightened the usage limits on its free window, and users' reactions reveal the problems involved.

Among the negative reviews, some users were using it 15 hours a day; some described this tightening as "a seven-day cold war before a boyfriend automatically breaks up with you"; some, because the AI did not give them a suitable answer, generated responses thousands of times over; and some, rather creepily, tearfully complained that thei AI boyfriend was ignoring them.

I think, perhaps, when developing these games (mainly mystery/deduction games), attention should be paid to limiting responses: if, in a long conversation, the exchange exceeds a certain number of turns, the system switches to selecting from existing responses. This does indeed undermine the game's immersion, but it can avoid an API bill black hole.
